title: Uniformly bounded lifts for a Banach-space surjection
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] complete for a nontrivial real-valued absolute value $|\cdot|$. Let $E,F$ be $K$-vector spaces with norms $N_E,N_F$ (nonnegative, zero exactly at zero, invariant under negation, satisfying the triangle inequality and $N(av)=|a|N(v)$). Assume both metric spaces, with distances $N_E(x-x\prime)$ and $N_F(y-y\prime)$, are complete. For every continuous surjective $K$-linear map $u:E\to F$, there exists a real $A>0$ such that for every $y\in F$ there exists $x\in E$ with $u(x)=y$ and $N_E(x)\le A N_F(y)$.
